counterevidence_considered.description: Potential concern probed: each stand's composite derives from four ingrowth bags (bags_pooled = 4), which could constitute repeated sub-unit measurements. However, the description states the bags were physically merged and weighed once before entering the file, so the sub-unit replication never appears as separate rows and cannot enter the test repeatedly; bags_pooled is constant bookkeeping, not a repeated measurement.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: bags_pooled = 4 on every row; pooling occurred before weighing

source_refs.quoted_text:
buried in the organic horizon in June and lifted in September. The four bags
from a stand were combined into a single composite sample in the field, and that
one composite was dried and weighed once in the laboratory. A stand therefore
yields exactly one ingrowth number, and it occupies exactly one line of the
file.

Nothing in the file is a repeated measurement of the same stand. The bags were
merged before weighing, so the file holds 24 measurements from 24 stands, and a
two-group comparison across rows compares independent stands.

evidence.description: The data description declares the stand as the independent unit, one row per stand, with stand_id unique across the file.
evidence.observed_value: One row = one stand; independent unit column stand_id; IDs ST-01 through ST-24 unique

source_refs.quoted_text:
One row is: one surveyed spruce stand, described by the single pooled ingrowth-bag composite collected in that stand
Independent unit column: stand_id
- stand_id: the code of the stand, unique across the file (ST-01 through ST-24).

evidence.description: The CSV contains exactly 24 data rows with 24 distinct stand_id values (ST-01 through ST-24); no stand occupies more than one row, so no independent unit enters the row-level test more than once. Verified by inspection of every row.
The workflow actively enforces one row per independent unit: read_stands raises a ValueError if any stand_id appears twice, so duplicated units cannot reach the test.
evidence.observed_value: Uniqueness guard on stand_id before analysis

evidence.description: The row-independent procedure (Welch two-sample t-test) is applied to the deduplicated stand-level rows, one value per stand per group (12 vs 12).
evidence.observed_value: stats.ttest_ind on 12 intact and 12 gap stand-level values

source_refs.quoted_text:
rows = read_stands(DATA_PATH)
    a = ingrowth(rows, REFERENCE)
    b = ingrowth(rows, CONTRAST)

evidence.description: The reported statistics are consistent with exactly one entry per stand: n = 12 per group (24 stands total), group means 41 and 28 mg match hand-computed means of the 12 unique stand values per group, and t = 6.5 with df = 22 follows from those 24 values.

source_refs.quoted_text: [selected-result] Welch's two-sample t-test on 12 intact-canopy stands versus 12 canopy-gap stands: mean difference 13.000 mg (intact minus gap), 95% CI [8.85, 17.15] mg, SE 2.000 mg, t = 6.5000, df = 22.00, two-sided p < 0.0001; mycelial ingrowth is higher in intact-canopy stands.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to demonstrate the issue by (1) scanning all 24 data rows of data/input.csv for any duplicated stand_id value — none exists, ST-01 through ST-24 each appear exactly once; (2) checking whether the workflow re-enters any row into the test (e.g., concatenation, per-bag expansion, or resampling) — ingrowth() filters the deduplicated rows once per group and stats.ttest_ind receives 12 and 12 values, and read_stands would raise on any duplicated stand_id; (3) checking whether the four bags per stand could act as repeated entries of the stand — the description states bags were physically pooled into one composite weighed once, so per-bag values never exist as rows; (4) recomputing the summary statistics from the 24 unique rows (intact mean 41, gap mean 28, difference 13, SE 2, t = 6.5, df = 22, both group SDs 4.899) — all match the report, which would not hold if any unit had been counted more than once. Every attempt failed to produce evidence of repeated independent-unit entry.
